chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who apostatized from Islam, [saying] 'To whom belongs his inheritance?' He said, 'It is divided among his heirs according to the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

key_terms.عَلَى كِتَابِ اَللَّهِ: According to the Book of Allah (Quran)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a man who apostatizes from Islam according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that an apostate's estate is divided among his heirs according to the general rules of the Quran, a view that distinguishes between the loss of the apostate's inheritance from others and the right of others to inherit from him. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it supports the position that apostasy does not sever kinship ties for inheritance purposes, contrasting with some Sunni schools that hold the apostate forfeits all inheritance. The phrase 'according to the Book of Allah' emphasizes the continuity of standard familial distribution rules despite the change in the individual's religious status.
